title: The Bee and Jupiter
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Queen Bee from Hymettus flew up to Olympus with some fresh honey from the hive as a present to Jupiter, who was so pleased with the gift that he promised to give her anything she liked to ask for. She said she would be very grateful if he would give stings to the bees, to kill people who robbed them of their honey. Jupiter was greatly displeased with this request, for he loved mankind: but he had given his word, so he said that stings they should have. The stings he gave them, however, were of such a kind that whenever a bee stings a man the sting is left in the wound and the bee dies.
Evil wishes, like fowls, come home to roost.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Queen Bee bring to Jupiter?
options: A newly built honeycomb
A gift of golden pollen
Some fresh honey from the hive
A swarm of young bees

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Jupiter promise the Queen Bee because he is so pleased?
options: To give her anything she likes to ask for
To visit the hive himself one day
To protect the hive from all storms
To make her honey taste even sweeter

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Queen Bee ask Jupiter for?
options: A larger hive to house more bees
Protection from birds that eat bees
The power to make honey more quickly
Stings for the bees, to kill people who steal their honey

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does Jupiter feel about the Queen Bee's request?
options: Delighted, since he disliked honey thieves
Greatly displeased, since he loved mankind
Indifferent, since it did not concern him
Amused, since he thought it a harmless wish

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does Jupiter grant the request despite his displeasure?
options: Because the other gods urged him to agree
Because he wanted more honey for himself
Because he had already given his word
Because the bees threatened to stop working

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to a bee after it stings a man?
options: The sting is left in the wound and the bee dies
The bee loses its ability to fly
The bee returns safely to the hive
The bee's sting grows back within a day

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Jupiter design the sting to cost the bee its own life?
options: He wants to make sure the bees cannot misuse the sting again
He is testing whether the bees will still want the gift
He hopes the bees will refuse the sting altogether
He shapes his reluctant gift so that the harmful wish also punishes the one who made it

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Jupiter's reluctant promise-keeping reveal about how he views his own word?
options: He breaks his promise once he realizes the request is harmful
He honors a promise even when he disapproves of what was asked
He asks the Queen Bee to choose a different gift instead
He delays his answer until the Queen Bee gives up asking

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "displeased" mean in "Jupiter was greatly displeased with this request"?
options: Delighted or thrilled
Confused or puzzled
Unhappy or dissatisfied
Indifferent or unmoved

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A wish for harm against others can end up bringing harm upon yourself
Gods should never grant requests they personally disagree with
Bees are naturally more vengeful than other creatures
Honey is valuable enough to justify any means of defending it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Queen Bee travel from to bring her gift?
options: Olympus itself
A distant island
The banks of a river
Hymettus

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Queen Bee want the stings used for?
options: To defend the hive from other insects
To kill people who steal the bees' honey
To help the bees gather pollen faster
To frighten away birds that hunt bees

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Jupiter feel toward mankind that explains his reaction?
options: Fear
Indifference
Love
Suspicion

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might Jupiter be seen as fair to both sides in how he grants the wish?
options: He gives the bees a weapon, but makes it cost them their own lives when used
He refuses the Queen Bee's request outright to protect mankind
He gives mankind a way to remove the bees' new stings
He asks the Queen Bee to apologize before granting anything

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Queen Bee fail to anticipate when making her request?
options: That Jupiter would refuse to grant any request at all
That mankind would stop stealing honey once warned
That the other gods would object to her wish
That the very gift she wanted could end up harming her own kind as well

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "robbed" mean in "people who robbed them of their honey"?
options: Warned
Stole
Shared
Sold

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Jupiter refuses the Queen Bee's request and sends her away empty-handed
The Queen Bee changes her mind and asks for something harmless instead
A wish for a weapon against others is granted in a form that punishes its user as well
Mankind negotiates directly with Jupiter to stop the bees' stings
